commenter_information.credentials_or_expertise_mentioned: National association representing health insurance plans covering over 205 million Americans across Medicare, Medicaid, employer-sponsored coverage, and the individual market.

executive_summary: AHIP supports extending electronic prior authorization requirements to drugs but argues that CMS must provide more implementation time, regulatory stability, and stronger provider adoption incentives. AHIP requests a 24-month post-final-rule compliance timeline, deferral of endpoint reporting, greater IG/version control, narrower and contextualized metrics, and alignment across payers, providers, vendors, CMS, ONC, and SDOs.

detailed_positions.rationale: Plans are still implementing non-drug ePA APIs for 2027 and need time to validate those workflows before adding drug-specific complexities, including medical/pharmacy benefit routing, PBM coordination, and delegated vendors.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Set compliance at 24 months after the final rule effective date rather than October 1, 2027.

detailed_positions.topic: Medical versus pharmacy benefit distinction and unified authorizations
detailed_positions.rationale: Providers may not know the correct benefit pathway at ordering, and rigid separation could fragment oncology and other regimen-level care.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Clarify benefit routing and permit unified prior authorizations for integrated regimens, protocols, and episodes of care.

detailed_positions.topic: Mandatory FHIR IGs and version management
detailed_positions.rationale: Specific versions, especially Da Vinci CRD/DTR/PAS 2.0, may be outdated or immature; IGs may impose policy beyond rulemaking and create version mismatch among payers, EHRs, and test tools.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Do not require specific CRD/DTR/PAS versions now; retain a named base FHIR standard; specify applicable IG capabilities by API; provide a stable transition framework and at least one additional year if specific versions are mandated.

detailed_positions.rationale: Payer investments will not reduce burden unless providers and EHR vendors adopt and use the API in production.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Move from attestation to performance-based measures, eventually consider a Medicare CoP, and align EHR certification and incentives with payer API requirements.

detailed_positions.rationale: There is no single national taxonomy across X12, CAQH, CMS, and proprietary codes; vendors need reconfiguration and testing time.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Set October 1, 2028 compliance, create an SDO-maintained denial reason taxonomy, issue detailed guidance, align with NCQA, and phase implementation where vendor constraints exist.

detailed_positions.rationale: Compressed timeframes without complete electronic submissions may increase denials, appeals, and patient safety risks.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Apply 24-hour response only for complete ePA submissions; measure timeframes from complete request receipt; allow clock pauses for missing information; make October 1, 2028 the earliest compliance date.

detailed_positions.rationale: Detailed metrics before APIs stabilize may be inconsistent and burdensome; raw counts can mislead because plan size differs.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Use narrow initial metrics, maintain percentages rather than raw counts, permit contextual narrative, and delay drug reporting changes until at least 2029 reporting using 2028 data.

detailed_positions.rationale: CMS has not fully explained legal authority, data scope, governance, PRA implications, publication format, validation, security risks, or how complex payer hierarchies will be represented.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Do not finalize mandatory endpoint reporting in this rule; issue a comprehensive proposed rule. If proceeding, use NDH Endpoint resources and clarify treatment of brands, affiliates, lines of business, delegates, and state-specific models.

detailed_positions.rationale: FHIR can modernize transactions, but broad HIPAA-covered entity adoption requires clear authority, phased implementation, coexistence rules, and alignment with X12/NCPDP workflows.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Finalize a carefully phased FHIR transition for prior authorization, avoid overbroad scope, and provide testing, guidance, and implementation flexibility.

detailed_positions.topic: ONC certification and payer API testing
detailed_positions.rationale: ONC can support testing, but formal payer certification may exceed statutory authority and create inappropriate information-blocking implications.
detailed_positions.specific_request: Support robust voluntary testing outside the statutory certification program, including test tools for all unexpired IG versions, technical assistance, and payer-focused forums.

solicitation_responses.summary: Supports standardization but opposes premature mandatory versions and requests clearer version control, API-specific capability scoping, and coordinated CMS/ONC transitions.
Drug ePA raises medical/pharmacy benefit routing, PBM coordination, and workflow issues; AHIP requests more time and flexibility for unified episode-level authorizations.
Requests alignment with NCPDP/PBM infrastructure, EHR vendor readiness, and continued exclusion of FFE stand-alone dental plans.
Supports clear denial reasons but requests a later date, national taxonomy, NCQA alignment, and guidance.
Opposes broad 24-hour decision timelines absent complete electronic submissions and requests clock pauses, complete-request definitions, and a later compliance date.
Requests deferral of endpoint reporting until CMS provides legal authority, governance, data scope, privacy/security protections, and PRA process.
Requests narrow, phased API usage metrics with privacy protections and enough implementation experience before detailed reporting.
Supports modernization but urges careful phasing, scope limits, testing, authority analysis, and coexistence/transition planning for FHIR-based HIPAA PA standards.
Requests predictable ONC standards updates, coordinated version transitions, and voluntary testing support rather than payer certification mandates.

key_quotes: Establish a compliance timeline of 24 months after the effective date of the final rule rather than a fixed calendar date.
Do not finalize payer endpoint reporting proposals at this time.
The full benefits of ePA will only be realized through widespread adoption by providers.
agency_action_requested: Finalize drug ePA in modified form with longer timelines, clearer version governance, stronger provider adoption incentives, deferred endpoint reporting, narrower metrics, and phased HIPAA/FHIR transition policies.
